summary.text: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, orbiting on an elliptical path that averages around 378,000 kilometers away.
Gravity between Earth and the Moon has pulled it so that the same near side always faces Earth.
It is thought to have formed from Earth material ejected by a giant impact of a Mars-sized body.

facts.label: Lunar month
facts.value: 29.5 days to orbit in relation to Earth and the Sun

facts.label: Visible surface
facts.value: About 59% can be seen from Earth

facts.label: First landing
facts.value: Humans reached the surface with Apollo 11 on July 20, 1969

items.prompt: What makes it possible for the Moon to cover the Sun completely during a total solar eclipse?

options.label: It is physically larger than the Sun is
Earth's shadow stretches out to the Sun
It looks about as big in Earth's sky as the Sun
Its bright surface scatters light over the Sun

items.explain: The Moon's apparent size in Earth's sky is about the same as the Sun's, so it can cover it completely.

items.prompt: Why do people on Earth always see the same near side of the Moon?

options.label: Its spin takes exactly as long as one orbit of Earth
It does not rotate and just drifts around Earth
Its far side is always hidden in Earth's shadow
The Sun's light only ever reaches its near side

items.explain: Tidal locking synchronizes the Moon's rotation period with its orbital period, so one side keeps facing Earth.

items.prompt: What are the maria, the patches long called 'seas', on the Moon's near side?

options.label: Dried-up ocean floors left by ancient water
Fields of fine dust gathered by impact blasts
Bright streaks thrown out by young craters
Basalt plains formed when lava filled old craters

items.explain: The Moon was volcanically active, and lava filled ancient craters and cooled into the dark basalt plains.

items.prompt: According to current thinking, how did the Moon come to exist?

options.label: Earth captured a passing planet that wandered by
A Mars-sized body hit Earth and flung out material
It condensed from the Sun's disc beside young Earth
Earth spun so fast that a chunk broke off

items.explain: The Moon is thought to have formed from Earth material ejected by a giant impact of a Mars-sized body.

items.prompt: The Moon's surface reflects light about as poorly as asphalt, yet it outshines every other object in Earth's night sky. Why?

options.label: Its dust glows with heat left over from old volcanoes
Its surface reflects more light than any planet does
It gives off its own light when impacts strike it
Its large apparent size makes up for a dull surface

items.explain: The Moon is the brightest object at night because of its large apparent size, even though its albedo is comparable to asphalt.

items.prompt: Although the same side always faces Earth, people can see more than half of the Moon's surface over time. Why?

options.label: The Moon slowly spins, turning new regions toward us
Earth's shadow covers less of the Moon each month
Shifting angles bring some of the far side into view
The Moon gets closer, so more of it fits in view

items.explain: Libration changes the angle at which the Moon appears in the sky, making parts of the far side visible.
